questions.question: Which membership statement about $\pi$ and $\mathbb{N}$ is true?
options: $\pi\in\mathbb{N}$
$\mathbb{N}\in\pi$
$\pi\notin\mathbb{N}$
$\pi = \mathbb{N}$

questions.question: Which statement correctly contrasts sets with ordered collections?
options: Sets order their elements from smallest to largest.
Sets keep the order in which elements are listed.
Sets record how often each element is repeated.
Sets do not impose order on their elements.

questions.question: Let $A=\{1,2,\{1\},\varnothing\}$. Which statement is false?
options: $\{1\}\in A$ and also $\{1\}\subseteq A$.
$\varnothing\in A$ and also $\varnothing\subseteq A$.
$\{2\}\subseteq A$ but $\{2\}\notin A$.

questions.question: Does $\{1,1,2\}$ equal $\{1,2\}$ as sets?
options: Yes; repeats do not create new elements.
No; the first set has three elements, the second two.
No; a set may not list the same element twice.
Yes, but only because both sets start with $1$.

questions.question: Which set is described by the notation $\{x\in\mathbb{R}\colon x>0\}$?
options: The set of all positive real numbers
The set of all non-negative real numbers
The set of all positive integers $1,2,3,\dots$
The set of all negative real numbers

questions.question: Which argument proves that two sets $A$ and $B$ are equal?
options: Show $A\subseteq B$ and $B\subseteq A$.
Show $A\subseteq B$; then $B\subseteq A$ follows.
Show that some element of $A$ also lies in $B$.
Show that $A$ and $B$ have the same number of elements.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about the size of sets?
options: Sets must always be finite.
Sets must have at least one element.
Only sets of integers can be infinite.
Sets may be finite or infinite.

questions.question: A student writes $x\notin A$. Which interpretation is correct?
options: $x$ is not a subset of the collection $A$.
$x$ lies in every set except $A$.
$x$ is not yet known to lie in $A$.
$x$ does not lie in the collection $A$.

questions.question: With the convention $0\in\mathbb{N}$, which listing describes the set $\{n\in\mathbb{N}\colon n^2<10\}$?
